camera.type: low fast tracking shot moving alongside the chase
camera.position: racing along the right-hand side of the muddy path (right-hand relative to the direction the animals travel) at knee height, only three to four meters from the Triceratops, keeping pace with it at full speed; it bounces hard and jolts with the rough ground, never smooth and floating
camera.framing: side-on to the chase, which moves toward the right of the frame: the juvenile Triceratops carrying Nora fills the right half of the frame; the tyrannosaur charges behind them in the left third of the frame; the forest background smears past from right to left with motion blur, and foreground ferns and branches whip across the lens about once every second, showing the speed

setting.location: Hell Creek floodplain forest, Montana, Late Cretaceous, 66 million years ago, humid late morning
elements: a dense, messy, irregular floodplain forest, never tidy or park-like: trees of many different ages and sizes, broadleaf trees and a few tall dawn redwoods, some trunks leaning, some broken and dead, fallen logs and rotting branches, hanging vines, moss and lichen on the bark, tangled leafy undergrowth and ferns of uneven height, leaf litter and puddles on uneven muddy ground; the trees are not evenly spaced
soft grey overcast daylight under the canopy, slightly underexposed in the shade, with brighter patches where the canopy opens; no sunbeams, no god rays, no visible light shafts

a shallow muddy stream crosses the path; at frame 0 the Triceratops is already bursting out of the stream onto the exit bank at full gallop, and the tyrannosaur is about twenty meters behind, charging into the stream from the far bank

exactly two dinosaurs and one person in the whole clip, all visible from frame 0: the Triceratops, Nora riding it, and exactly one tyrannosaur; no second tyrannosaur ever appears; no other animals, no birds in the frame, no other people; nothing enters the frame from the right edge or the foreground, especially in the last two seconds; nothing appears from nowhere and nothing vanishes

characters.name: Nora
characters.visual_lock: matches Nora face and Nora Body reference images exactly; honey-blonde hair tied in a high ponytail at the crown of her head, wispy curtain bangs parted in the middle
characters.outfit: wears the exact historical outfit shown in the Nora Body reference sheet: golden-tan deer suede tunic with long sleeves that reach all the way to her wrists (never sleeveless), wide dark belt, golden-tan suede leggings the same color as the tunic that cover her legs completely from hips to boots, and criss-cross laced knee boots; no bare skin on her thighs, knees or shins at any moment (NO shearling collar, NO extra fur, NO hood, NO fringe, NO tassels, NO outfit variations); even while she rides astride with her knees apart, the golden-tan suede leggings cover her thighs completely all the way up to the tunic hem, with no gap of skin between the tunic hem and the boots
characters.action: rides astride the Triceratops just behind its frill, crouched low over its neck; for the whole clip both hands grip the frill rim and never let go, even while she talks; her knees clamp its flanks, her body jolts hard with every stride and her ponytail streams behind her; she looks back over her right shoulder, toward the camera side, at the tyrannosaur while she speaks, so her face and mouth stay visible to the camera

characters.name: Juvenile Triceratops
characters.visual_lock: matches the Juvenile Triceratops reference image exactly: pony-sized, olive-brown pebbly hide with darker mottled bands, short brow horns curving backward, a short rounded frill edged with small triangular bumps
characters.position: gallops flat out to the right along the path with Nora on its back for the whole clip: legs pumping so fast they blur, head low, frill bobbing, mud spraying back in long streaks; it never turns and never slows; its back is about as high as Nora's waist when she stands

characters.name: Tyrannosaur
characters.visual_lock: matches the Tyrannosaurus reference image exactly: massive boxy skull, tiny two-fingered forearms, dark grey-brown pebbly hide with faint darker stripes and a paler belly, long tail held straight out level
characters.position: charges after them along the same path at its top speed and stays behind them for the whole clip: its head never passes the Triceratops's tail and it never comes alongside; more than twice as tall as the Triceratops: its hips are higher than the top of the Triceratops's frill with Nora on top; it moves with long, powerful, ground-eating strides, body pitched forward and tail straight out, but it never leaves the ground: one foot is always on the ground; its mouth is closed with scaly lips over the teeth except during the roar

timeline_action.0-3s: From frame 0 the Triceratops is already bursting out of the stream at full gallop, water exploding off its legs, and races to the right; the tyrannosaur charges into the stream about twenty meters behind, each huge stride throwing up a wall of brown water. Nora shouts from second 0, bouncing hard.
timeline_action.3-7s: The tyrannosaur bursts out of the stream onto the path and keeps charging at its top speed, still about twenty meters behind in the left third of the frame. From about 3.5 to 5 seconds it lifts its head and opens its jaws wide in one long roar mid-stride while Nora goes silent and flattens herself against the frill; its jaws close by 5 seconds. Then Nora looks back over her right shoulder and shouts again. The Triceratops gallops flat out to the right.
timeline_action.7-10s: Both animals tear along the muddy path at full speed, the tyrannosaur still about twenty meters behind in the left third of the frame, never closer; foreground ferns whip across the lens. Nora finishes her line by about 9 seconds; the last half second is only the flat-out gallop. In the final frame: the Triceratops with Nora in the right half, the same single tyrannosaur small in the left third, nothing else in the frame.

motion_choreography.frame0_state: Side-on fast tracking view: the Triceratops with Nora is bursting out of the stream onto the exit bank in the right half of the frame, water exploding off its legs; the tyrannosaur is about twenty meters behind in the left third, charging into the stream from the far bank.

speech.speaker: Nora
speech.voice_profile: Laomedeia, breathless and panicked, rising into a cracking shout in danger, then a relieved laugh

segments.0-3s: Go, go, go! Faster, big guy, faster!
segments.3-7s: It's out of the water, it's coming!
segments.7-10s: Don't stop, don't stop, keep running, we can make it!

delivery.0-3s: Nora shouts (breathless, frantic, bouncing with each stride)
delivery.3-7s: Nora stays silent during the roar, then screams (panicked, high and cracking)

speech.dialogue: Go, go, go! Faster, big guy, faster! It's out of the water, it's coming! Don't stop, don't stop, keep running, we can make it!

audio.ambience: rushing wind and forest, low under her voice
audio.sfx: pounding footfalls, splashing and mud spray from both animals, low under her voice; one long deep tyrannosaur roar from 3.5 to 5 seconds while Nora is silent

physical_realism.force_and_traction: both animals are enormously heavy and moving at full speed: every footfall smashes into the mud and throws it back in long streaks; water explodes off their legs in the stream; the tyrannosaur's huge strides shake the ground; the Triceratops's shoulders drive up and down hard under the rider
physical_realism.secondary_motion: Nora's ponytail streams back and whips with every stride; mud clods fly; leaves and ferns whip aside and spring back; the tyrannosaur's tail sways against each stride
physical_realism.environment: muddy water churning brown, droplets flying, wet leaves trembling as the animals pass
physical_realism.camera_response: the tracking view bounces hard and jolts as it races alongside, with strong motion blur on the background; it never floats smoothly; foreground plants whip across the lens about once every second
physical_realism.documentary_texture: real camera footage: slight motion blur on the fast-moving legs, focus that lags a fraction behind the moving animals, exposure that shifts as the camera passes from shade into brighter gaps, faint natural noise in the shadows, foreground ferns and branches whipping past very close to the lens and briefly blurring the frame edge; matte, wet, mud-caked scaly hides; looks like real footage of living animals, not CGI, not a video game, not a 3D render, not toys

negative_constraints: no god rays, no volumetric light beams, no lens flare, no light orbs, no colored light spots anywhere in the frame
the forest is never tidy, evenly spaced or park-like
the camera lens and any recording gear are completely outside the visible frame and never seen
the tyrannosaur never touches the Triceratops or Nora, never comes alongside, and its head never passes the Triceratops's tail; it stays about twenty meters behind for the whole clip
exactly one tyrannosaur for the whole clip; no second tyrannosaur ever appears; nothing enters the frame from the right edge or the foreground, especially in the last two seconds
the tyrannosaur never turns around and never spins; it keeps facing the way it travels
the tyrannosaur never leaps, never falls over and never has both feet off the ground; its teeth show only while its jaws are open for the roar
Nora stays seated on the Triceratops for the whole clip and never falls; both her hands stay on the frill rim
exactly two dinosaurs and one person; no other animals and no other people
no snow, no frost, no winter
no subtitles, no text on screen, no watermark
no morphing or vanishing animals, people or objects
no metal, no modern items anywhere in the frame
the animals look like real heavy living animals, never like plastic toys, rubber models or animatronics
no character stands frozen or statue-like at any moment
no slow motion; the chase is at full real-time speed
